Big news. We are joining Y Combinator 's W26 batch!! One year ago, we interviewed for W25 and were flatly rejected. This really sucked, because we felt how badly we screwed up the interview. It didn't even last the full 10 minutes. Cathleen Kuo, MD and I both had this sinking feeling in our stomach immediately after. Our biggest mistake was trying to pitch a long term vision for our company that wasn't really grounded in reality. We thought investors wanted to hear "big and grand" visions so they could return their fund. Maybe that works for some investors, but not for YC. YC mostly cares about fundamentals. Stuff like: - What are you building? - Who's using it? - Why do they use it? - Who are the founders? (We found this YC interview practice site super helpful: https://lnkd.in/gbwqkv4W ). When we interviewed again for YC in-person at their SF office a few weeks ago, we did the opposite of what we did last time. We just answered the questions simply - succinct, crisp, and no fluff. That same night at 10pm, we got a FaceTime from our YC partner inviting us to join the W26 batch. We were ecstatic. I probably woke up my neighbors with the elated scream I let out after we hung up the FaceTime. For anyone applying to YC in future batches: Build a fundamentally strong company and be able to explain it clearly in 10 minutes. No amount of fluff or buzzwords will get you in. If anything, you LOSE points by not being concise and sharp. I'm incredibly proud of our little team and grateful to everyone who's helped us get here. Your life can change really, really fast. Keep going.

Are you a student who wants to learn how VC ✨actually✨ works? Come intern at Khosla Ventures this fall! You'll be in a dual software + operations role working directly with one of our legendary MDs. Specific details will be shared with applicants directly 👀 I often find college students spinning on what to work on since they lack purview into the real world. Taking a semester/quarter off is a scary leap: folks may tell you to focus on studies, you'll have to speak up in rooms with folks decades older than you. But being in the real world is, in my opinion, the only way you can chose the best work vector. I took time off in college to found the company that changed my life. At the time, everyone thought I was nuts. But in retrospect, its one of the best decisions I ever made. Requirements: ✨ Know basic RAG and fullstack software principles. ✨ Be that unicorn that can code but also loves yapping for the operations side. ✨ Work from our Menlo Park office 5 days a week. ✨ Be a chiller like Harsh Singh because you'll be stuck in the office next to mine and I want to like you as a human. ✨ Tbh have a ton of confidence. You'll have exposure to venture both inside and outside KV with some very high level folks. You must be able to hold your own in a room with anyone. 👉 Know someone who’s a fit? Drop a comment or DM me!

We’re excited to share that Tilde completed an $8M seed round earlier this year, led by Khosla Ventures , with participation from Forgepoint Capital , Soma Capital , Timeless , and Bain Capital Ventures , as well as individual backing from researchers at OpenAI and Anthropic. Understanding model intelligence is the most important problem in the world, and the key to actualizing the promise that ASI can offer. Most current ML research takes a phenomenological approach, hillclimbing on real and synthetic tasks through extensive trial and error. Interpretability, by contrast, offers the powerful unlock of reverse-engineering and deeply analyzing systems to reveal their internal mechanisms. At Tilde, we believe in uniting these two perspectives. Interpretability shouldn't be an afterthought: it should inform how we train, deploy, and interface with models from the start. We recently reverse-engineered sparse attention mechanisms (MoBA, NSA) to understand *why* they outperform full attention: https://lnkd.in/eARbdcbs This is just a step. Our mission is to make interpretability a *driving force* in building more capable systems. If this resonates, come work with us: https://lnkd.in/eUCEYJmx We are actively hiring for founding members of technical staff across engineering and research roles
